transcript.text: Samsung WW90T534DAW keeps coming up with 4C after a couple of minutes. Drum is dry. Any ideas before I call someone out?

Yes — a Samsung 4C code means the machine is not detecting enough incoming water. With the drum still dry after a couple of minutes, start with the supply rather than a drain or drum fault. Check that the cold-water isolation tap feeding the washer is fully open and that the inlet hose is not kinked or trapped behind the machine. If both are fine, switch off and unplug the machine, turn off the tap, then check the small mesh filter at the hose connection for debris (have a towel ready); a blocked mesh is a common free fix. If water supply and the mesh are clear but 4C returns, the inlet valve or its control will need an engineer.
Tap was open, I turned it fully anticlockwise anyway and no change. Hose isn't kinked. Kitchen cold tap pressure is normal. I'll try the mesh filter next.

The mesh filter is now the most likely free fix. Switch the machine off and unplug it, turn the water tap off, put a towel underneath, then unscrew the inlet hose from the back of the washer. Look into the machine’s inlet connection for the small mesh screen; rinse loose debris off it gently without pushing it into the valve or damaging it. Refit the hose securely, turn the tap back on and try a programme. If the mesh is already clean and it still remains completely dry with 4C, the inlet water valve becomes the leading suspect and would normally need an engineer to test and replace.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the fill-hose mesh filter is" — A small mesh filter sits inside the fill-hose connector at the tap/valve end and catches grit. Turn the tap off, unscrew the hose and rinse the mesh. Typical layout — your machine may differ.]
Done it. The mesh filter was clogged with grey grit and limescale bits. Cleaned it, refitted the hose and it fills normally now, 4C has gone.
That has fixed it: the clogged inlet mesh was restricting the water supply and triggering the 4C code. The grey grit and scale are common causes. Is there anything else you would like help with?

candidates: Water tap closed/restricted or poor water supply (high)
Kinked inlet hose or blocked inlet mesh filter (medium)

Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
